title: Integrating ORNL's HPC and Neutron Facilities with a Performance-Portable CPU/GPU Ecosystem
problem: Data reduction workflows at the Spallation Neutron Source must efficiently compute differential scattering cross-sections from CORELLI and TOPAZ instruments. The current CPU-only production implementation using Mantid C++ lacks cross-platform performance portability for integration with HPC systems.
motivation: Integrating DOE's experimental facilities with leadership computing resources requires software that maintains performance across heterogeneous CPU and GPU architectures.
method: The team reimplemented the core algorithms from the production software (Mantid C++) in Julia, a scientific computing language, using JACC.jl—a library that automatically optimizes code to run on both CPUs and graphics processors without rewriting it for each hardware type. Two test applications were created—MDNorm in C++ and MiniVATES.jl in Julia—to compare the new approach against the original Mantid C++ production code. Performance was measured on real hardware: NVIDIA A100 and AMD MI100 graphics processors paired with AMD EPYC 7513/7662 CPUs.
key_novelty: One data reduction program in Julia and JACC.jl replaces separate CPU and GPU implementations, running efficiently on both hardware types.
contributions: Performance-portable CPU/GPU ecosystem for integrating HPC and scientific instrument facilities
Direct performance comparison of Mantid Python/C++ versus Julia-based approaches for data reduction
Proxy applications demonstrating feasibility of performance-portable data reduction
Multi-architecture evaluation across NVIDIA A100, AMD MI100 GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs
